title: Your first game: play four moves
outcomes: Plays the marked moves of a short real game and sees a capture, a check and a checkmate happen
Says that pieces attack by moving to where they could capture, before knowing the full rules

steps.title: A real game, in four moves

moves.say: Your pawn steps forward two squares and claims the centre.
moves.hint: The pawn in front of your king.

moves.say: Your bishop slides out along a diagonal and looks at the f7 pawn.
moves.hint: The bishop next to your king.

moves.say: Black develops a knight and does not notice the bishop's aim.
Your queen swings out and now looks at f7 as well.
moves.hint: The queen goes up the board to h5.

moves.say: Black attacks your queen, but the f7 pawn is still only guarded by the king.
Your queen captures on f7. The king is attacked and has no safe square: checkmate.
moves.hint: Capture the pawn on f7 with the queen.

steps.end: You just won a game. Black helped by missing the threat, and you will soon see how to stop it. Next: how the board is named, so you can talk about any square.

steps.text: That was a **real game**, and it ended in **checkmate**: the king was attacked and Black had no legal answer: no move away, capture or block. You captured a pawn, gave a check and won, using only a pawn, a bishop and a queen. Strong players do not lose this way, because they notice a piece aiming at f7. Learning to notice is what the next lessons are for.

steps.caption: The moment before the finish. White to move: the queen and the bishop both aim at the f7 pawn, and Black's king has nowhere to run.

line.say: The queen takes the pawn with check. The bishop guards her, so the king cannot capture, and every square around him is blocked by his own pieces. That is checkmate.

steps.text: That four-move checkmate has a name: **Scholar's Mate**. It is where this app gets its name too: a *scholar* is someone who studies, and a *mate* is both a checkmate and a study partner. Scholarmate is a place to study with a friend, and you have already played your first checkmate.

steps.prompt: Which two pieces were both aiming at the f7 pawn before the queen captured it?

sources: Written 8 Nov 2026 for the first-ten-minutes promise (docs/first-game-design.md); wording original. The move order is replayed legally by tools/validate_lessons.py; the claim that Black misses the threat is a fact of this line, not a claim about strong play.
